samples.summary: Removing `href` from CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE drops the only bulk way to strip untrusted hrefs from pasted/imported content (defense-in-depth only; every consumer still gates on isSafeUrl)
samples.evidence: HTML paste and clipboard deserialization store an arbitrary `href` string into the model without any scheme check: `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:610-612` (`const href = el.getAttribute('href'); if (href) style.href = href;`) and `sanitizeInlineStyle` at `clipboard.ts:148-149` (`const href = asString(value.href); if (href !== undefined) style.href = href;`). Before this change, selecting the pasted region and running Clear formatting removed those hrefs wholesale, because `href: undefined` was in `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`. After the diff (types.ts hunk removing `href: undefined`), a `javascript:`/`data:text/html` href pasted from a hostile page — or arriving from a collaborator through the Yorkie store (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:139/194` round-trips `href` verbatim) — survives Clear formatting, and the only removal command is `removeLink`, which acts on one link at a time (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3719`). I traced every href consumer I could find and all of them do gate: click-to-open (`text-editor.ts:1822` and `:2176` both `isSafeUrl(href)` before `window.open`), the link popover anchor (`docs-link-popover.tsx:217,224`), markdown export (`serialize/markdown.ts:248` `isEmittableUrl`), PDF annotations (`export/pdf-painter.ts:854,902`), and PPTX export (`slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:273`). So this is not an exploitable XSS today — it is a reduction of defense in depth plus a user-visible loss of the 'nuke everything I just pasted' escape hatch. Hardening: sanitize `href` at paste/import time (reuse `@wafflebase/core/url` `isSafeUrl`) so unsafe schemes never enter the model, rather than relying on every present and future consumer to re-check.
searchedFor: grep style.href in packages/frontend/src and packages/slides/src/view

samples.summary: New Remove-link toolbar button carries no read-only/permission gate of its own; it relies solely on the shared `disabled` prop and on text-edit mode being unreachable for viewers
samples.evidence: The new button (text-format-group.tsx:310-323) is rendered whenever `showRemoveLink` is set and is only disabled via `isDisabled = disabled || !editor` (line 186); `handleRemoveLink` (line 174-178) calls `editor.removeLink?.()` unconditionally. Unlike the docs link popover, which explicitly guards its unlink control behind `!readOnly` (docs-link-popover.tsx:231), the slides call sites (`toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:93`, `toolbar/mobile-toolbar.tsx:580`) pass `showRemoveLink` with no read-only plumbing — `grep readOnly packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar` returns nothing. I could not build an exploit chain: slides mounts the editor with `readOnly: readOnlyMount` (slides-view.tsx:722) and the text-edit toolbar section only renders while text editing is active, which a read-only mount should never enter (slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1123 gates handler wiring on `!options.readOnly`), and the mutation itself would still have to pass server-side document permissions. Reporting as a hardening note: this button is a document-mutating action whose only authorization is 'the toolbar happened not to render', identical to its sibling formatting buttons, so if that assumption is ever weakened it fails open silently.
searchedFor: grep readOnly in text-edit-section.tsx and mobile-toolbar.tsx
